ca_dome_rock.blurb: A big dome of solid granite in the Kern River Sierra, below Slate Mountain and close to the Western Divide Highway. The top is broad and flat, with views across the river canyon toward the Kern Plateau and The Needles. Most of the 24 climbs here are trad, with a few bolted lines and a couple of top-ropes. Grades start around 5.6 and reach the low 5.12s, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.11. Some lines are old-style slab climbs with thin footwork and sparse protection, so the crag suits leaders who are comfortable placing their own gear. Walls that face south can heat up by midday.

ca_intersection_rock_climbs.blurb: Intersection Rock is the most-climbed formation in Joshua Tree National Park, a huge dollop of quartz monzonite beside Hidden Valley Campground just off Park Boulevard. It has many faces and well over forty routes in total. The 24 climbs here are mostly trad, with seven boulder problems from VB to V4 and a couple of top-ropes. Roped grades run from easy fifth class up to 5.12, with plenty in the 5.8 to 5.9 range alongside a solid group at 5.11 and 5.12. Easy cracks and chimneys make it a handy place to learn, and it is a popular spot to watch other climbers.
ca_intersection_rock_climbs.parking_note: Leave the car in the paved lot right beside the rock, just off Park Boulevard near Hidden Valley Campground.

ca_middle_spire.blurb: Middle Spire is a granite tower in the Phantom Spires group on the Highway 50 corridor near Lake Tahoe, at roughly 6,000 feet. It is the busiest and easiest to reach of the spires. The rock is friction-dependent and often knobby, with terrain from very slabby to moderately overhanging. Of the 24 routes here, most are trad and a handful are bolted, running from about 5.6 to 5.11 with the heaviest cluster in the 5.7 to 5.10 range. The spire stands in an open field, so sun shifts around it through the day, and the west side can be windy. Every route finishes with a rappel.

ca_campfire_crag_south_face.blurb: The south face of Campfire Crag is part of a massive formation west of Pixie Rock in Joshua Tree National Park, at around 3,200 feet. It faces the sun, which makes it a good pick on cold, windy days. The 24 climbs are mostly trad (14), with seven sport lines and three top-ropes on coarse, friction-rich granite. Grades run from roughly 5.6 to 5.11, with most between 5.6 and 5.10, so there is a fair amount for newer leaders. The crag sees a fraction of the traffic of the nearby Feudal Wall, Short Wall and Pixie Rock.

ca_k_public_sanitation_wall.blurb: A sport-leaning wall on the south side of Yosemite Valley, found along Southside Drive at about 4,400 feet. It is split into a lower and an upper tier, with featured, slightly overhanging granite and single-pitch lines. Of the 24 climbs, 17 are bolted and seven are trad. Almost everything is 5.10 or harder: the bulk sits at 5.11 and 5.12, with just one at 5.13. That makes it a spot for strong climbers who want hard face climbing without a big commitment, rather than a place for beginners.

ca_cougar_crag_east.blurb: The east side of Cougar Crag, a low-elevation granodiorite crag in north San Diego County about a mile east of Interstate 15 on Highway 76. The crag is mostly sunny with some evening shade. The 24 climbs here are a mix of sport (15), trad (6), top-rope and a couple of boulder problems. Roped routes run from about 5.6 to 5.11, and many fall between 5.9 and 5.10c, so it suits intermediate leaders well. The East side has the more bolted lines, while the neighbouring West side holds more of the older trad climbs.

ca_lower_tier_left_side.blurb: The left-hand section of the Lower Tier at Frustration Creek, one of the Highway 38 crags in the San Bernardino Mountains, at about 4,800 feet. The climbing is on featured granite in a rocky slot canyon, where sun and shade are both available. Of the 24 routes, 21 are sport and three are trad, including a few multi-pitch lines. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.13a, with the largest group at 5.10 to 5.12. Some of the newer routes still have loose rock, so helmets and care are sensible.
ca_lower_tier_left_side.approach: A climber trail drops down from the road; the routes begin around a large oak tree and continue leftward toward a waterfall.
